model.name: Meeting / Session
model.purpose: Provide the context an agent needs to convene, run, observe and hand off a single meeting or session occurrence — identity, convening basis, timing, setting, participation, agenda, conduct, outcomes and record obligations — without owning the durable records, the convening body or the parties it references.
model.scope_statement: WM-ACT-025 models one bounded occurrence in which two or more parties are convened, synchronously or in mixed mode, to transact business under a shared agenda. It covers the occurrence from convocation to close: how it is identified and classified, on whose authority it was called, when and where it takes place, who was invited and who was actually present, what was on the agenda, what procedural acts and votes occurred, what outcomes were reached, what was captured during the session, how open the session was, and which durable records it owes. It deliberately stops at the boundary of the artefacts it produces and the actors it references: minutes and transcripts (WM-REC-012), decision records (WM-REC-010), the convening body (WM-ORG-018), parties, places, tasks and documents are referenced with subject-specific binding parameters only. The model is storage- and interface-neutral; iCalendar, JSCalendar, schema.org, XCON and vendor conferencing objects are alignments and projections, not the semantics.
in_scope: Identity, classification and revision of a single meeting or session occurrence, including its position in a recurring series.
Binding to the convening authority and the convocation notice, with the sufficiency tests attached to that notice.
Planned and observed timing, suspension and resumption, rescheduling, postponement and cancellation of the occurrence.
Physical setting, virtual conferencing endpoints, mixed-mode equivalence, reserved resources and accessibility provision.
Invited and actual participation: roles, invitation response state, delegation and proxy, presence observation and recusal.
Quorum determination at this occurrence, measured against a threshold rule owned by the convening body.
Agenda composition, adoption, amendment, deferral and carry-over, with references to tabled papers.
Conduct of proceedings: procedural acts, speaking-turn management, motions, voting method, tally and declared result.
Outcomes reached and follow-up assignments, expressed as references to the records and tasks that carry them.
In-session capture (recording, live transcription) with notification and consent basis, and the obligation to produce durable records.
Openness and closure of the session or its portions, observer admission, and the inventory of session-held personal data.
Declarative alignment to calendar, event and conferencing vocabularies.
out_of_scope: Drafting, approval, authenticity, publication and disposition of the minutes or transcript — owned by WM-REC-012; 'approval of the minutes' appears here only as an agenda item of a later session.
Content, status, rationale, supersession and implementation tracking of decision records — owned by WM-REC-010.
Composition, mandate, terms of reference, standing membership, chair designation rules and delegated powers of the convening body — owned by WM-ORG-018.
Master identity, contact data and affiliation of persons and organisations — owned by the adopting Dimension's party models.
Master data for places, buildings and rooms — only the reference and a local room designation are held here.
Generic occurrence semantics shared by all activities — owned by the parent model WM-ACT-018.
Execution and completion lifecycle of assigned actions — owned by the task model.
Version and custody management of tabled papers — owned by the document model.
Runtime evaluation and enforcement of access decisions, and storage of audit trails; this model carries classifications and references to audit events only.
Operation of calendaring transport (iTIP, CalDAV) and conferencing media transport, floor-control protocol mechanics and codec negotiation.
Decisions taken without a meeting (written resolutions, silence or written procedure) where no session occurrence exists.
Meeting-effectiveness analytics, sentiment scoring and engagement metrics.

boundary_notes.distinction: This model records that a record is owed, which content the applicable regime requires, who must produce and certify it, and which agenda item each passage anchors to. The record's own draft, approval, correction, authenticity and disposition lifecycle belongs to WM-REC-012.

Putting a question, the voting method, the tally and the declaration of the result are session conduct and are modelled here. The durable decision with its rationale, status, supersession and implementation is carried by WM-REC-010 and referenced by identifier.

Quorum thresholds, membership, voting entitlement and delegated powers are properties of the body's constitution. This model records only the determination made at this occurrence and the officer who presided over it.

Generic occurrence identity, scheduling status and cancellation semantics common to all activities are inherited from the parent. This model specialises only the deliberative surface: agenda, quorum, motions, capture and record obligation.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Party models for persons and organisations
boundary_notes.distinction: Participants are references. Role, invitation response, presence intervals and recusal are occurrence-scoped facts held here; names, addresses and affiliations are not mastered here.
The model classifies openness, marks closed portions and stores references to audit events raised elsewhere. It does not evaluate authorisation, enforce it, or hold the audit trail.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Conferencing platform (XCON model or vendor service)
boundary_notes.distinction: Conference object state, admission policy enforcement, floor control and media handling are the platform's runtime concern. This model binds the conference object identifier, the published endpoints and the exported attendance observations.
iCalendar, JSCalendar and schema.org Event are alignments. Mappings are recorded with their lossy points; no conformance is claimed and no format is required by the semantics.

bundles.name: Session constitution and convening basis
bundles.description: What this occurrence is, how it is identified and classified, and the authority and notice under which it exists.
bundles.rationale: Nothing else about a meeting is interpretable until the occurrence is uniquely identifiable, correctly classified for the procedural regime that applies to it, and traceable to a party entitled to convene it. Statutory open-meeting and company-law regimes attach their obligations to exactly these facts.

layers.name: Identity and classification
layers.description: Stable identification of the occurrence across systems and revisions, and the classification axes that select the applicable obligations.

findings.name: Occurrence identity and revision resolution
findings.description: How one meeting occurrence is distinguished from its series, from its own earlier revisions, and from copies of it held in other systems.

questions.text: Which authoritative master-system identifier designates this occurrence, and which governed global identifier is published for it?
answer_data: Master-system meeting identifier and the name of the issuing system of record
Governed global identifier or IRI published for the occurrence
Flag stating which identifier is authoritative where both exist

questions.text: How is a single occurrence distinguished from its recurring series when both carry the same identifier?
answer_data: Recurrence instance discriminator with its own time zone reference

questions.text: Which revision counter and timestamp determine which copy of the meeting definition prevails when two differ?
Which external system identifiers are bound to this occurrence, and which of them may be treated as authoritative?

data_elements.name: Session identifier
data_elements.description: Authoritative identifier of the occurrence, assigned by the identity priority of the adopting Dimension.

data_elements.name: Series identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the recurring series that generated this occurrence, where one exists.

data_elements.name: Recurrence instance key
data_elements.description: Discriminator that selects this occurrence within its series, expressed as the original scheduled start with its time zone.

data_elements.name: Revision sequence
data_elements.description: Monotonic counter incremented when the convener changes the definition of the occurrence.

data_elements.name: Definition updated at
data_elements.description: Instant at which the current revision of the definition was created.

data_elements.name: External identifier binding
data_elements.description: Bound identifiers held by other systems for the same occurrence, each with its authority flag.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Identity is reference data carried on the occurrence entry itself: identifiers, a revision counter, a revision instant and a binding map. No document, media object or issued instrument is produced by resolving identity, and materialising one would create a second competing identifier space.

Code list reference and its governing register

questions.text: Is the session conducted in person, online or in a mixed mode, and which mode applies to each participant?

data_elements.name: Meeting type code
data_elements.description: Governed code identifying the procedural class of the occurrence.

data_elements.name: Attendance mode

data_elements.name: Openness class

data_elements.name: Classification basis reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the rule, statute or terms of reference that fixes the classification.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Classification is a small set of coded values plus a pointer to the instrument that fixes them. The instrument itself is a document owned by another model, so declaring an artifact here would duplicate the governing body's rule set rather than describe the occurrence.

Interval of the session over which each officer presided

data_elements.name: Convening body reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the governance body or office that convened the occurrence.

data_elements.name: Convening instrument reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the rule, statute or terms of reference conferring the power to convene.

data_elements.name: Presiding officer reference
data_elements.description: Party reference for the officer presiding, with the interval presided over.

data_elements.name: Requisition basis
data_elements.description: Statement of who requested the session and against which threshold.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The mandate, membership and delegated powers that make the convening act valid are owned by WM-ORG-018. This finding therefore holds only pointers and occurrence-scoped parameters; issuing an artifact here would reproduce the body's constitutional documents inside a session record.

findings.name: Notice and convocation
findings.description: The act of announcing the session to those entitled to attend or observe, and the sufficiency tests that attach to that announcement.

questions.text: What notice was issued, to whom, through which channel, and how long before the session?
answer_data: Lead duration between issue and planned start

questions.text: Does the applicable regime require public announcement, and which content must that announcement carry?
answer_data: Public announcement required flag and its legal basis
Mandatory content elements (time, place, subject matter, open or closed status, contact person)

questions.text: What is the consequence for the validity of business transacted if the notice period or content requirement was not met?
Which post-issuance changes require an amended or re-issued notice?
answer_data: Reference from amended notice to the superseded one

data_elements.description: Instant at which the convocation notice was issued or published.

data_elements.name: Notice channel
data_elements.description: Channel through which the notice was communicated or published.

data_elements.name: Notice lead duration
data_elements.description: Interval between notice issuance and the planned start.

data_elements.name: Notice defect note
data_elements.description: Recorded defect in notice and the curative step taken.

artifacts.name: Meeting notice or convocation
artifacts.description: The issued announcement of the session carrying time, place or access channel, subject matter, openness status and contact point.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Notice identifier assigned by the issuing secretariat or, where a public register is used, the register's published notice identifier, which is authoritative; the notice always carries the session identifier and the revision sequence current at issue.

bundles.name: Time, series position and setting
bundles.description: When the occurrence is scheduled and observed, where it sits in a series, and the physical, virtual and accessibility conditions under which it takes place.
bundles.rationale: A session is bounded in time and place, and both the planned and the observed values carry procedural weight. Calendaring standards fix the time and recurrence semantics, conferencing standards fix the access channel, and accessibility guidance fixes the conditions for equivalent participation.

layers.name: Timing, series position and schedule change
layers.description: Planned and observed temporal extent, recurrence position, and the transitions that move or end the occurrence.

findings.name: Planned and observed timing
findings.description: The scheduled temporal extent of the occurrence and the times actually observed for opening, suspension, resumption and close.

questions.text: What are the planned start and end of the session, and in which named time zone were they expressed?
answer_data: Planned end instant or planned duration

questions.text: What actual opening, suspension, resumption and closing times were observed, and by which observer?
answer_data: Observation or ingestion instant where it differs from the event instant

questions.text: Which time value governs a procedural deadline when the planned and observed times diverge?
How are all-day, open-ended and multi-day sessions bounded in this model?
answer_data: Treatment of overnight adjournment as one occurrence or several
Rule for sessions with no scheduled end

data_elements.name: Planned start
data_elements.description: Scheduled start of the occurrence.

data_elements.name: Planned end
data_elements.description: Scheduled end of the occurrence, where a planned duration is not used instead.

data_elements.name: Scheduling time zone
data_elements.description: Named time zone in which the planned times were expressed, retained alongside the offset.

data_elements.name: Observed open at
data_elements.description: Instant at which the session was actually opened.

data_elements.name: Observed close at
data_elements.description: Instant at which the session was actually closed or adjourned sine die.

data_elements.name: Suspension interval
data_elements.description: Intervals during which proceedings were suspended and later resumed.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Timing is a set of instants, a named zone and observation metadata held directly on the occurrence. Any document that carries these values is either the notice or the durable record, both of which are modelled elsewhere, so no separate artifact belongs to this finding.

findings.name: Series membership and recurrence position
findings.description: Whether the occurrence was generated by a recurrence rule, what it inherits from the series, and how it relates to the sessions before and after it.

questions.text: Was this occurrence generated by a recurrence rule, and what rule expression produced it?
Which properties of this occurrence override the series definition and which remain inherited?
How is an occurrence detached from its series, and what identity does it carry afterwards?
answer_data: Residual link to the former series

questions.text: Which sessions immediately precede and follow this one for the purpose of carrying business over?

data_elements.name: Recurrence rule expression
data_elements.description: Rule that generated the occurrence within its series.

data_elements.name: Series reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the series or superordinate event of which this is an instance.

data_elements.name: Instance override flag
data_elements.description: Whether this occurrence differs from the series-generated default.

data_elements.name: Adjacent session reference
data_elements.description: References to the preceding and following occurrences in the series.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Series position is expressed entirely as rule text, references and an override flag. Materialising a series as an artifact would either duplicate the parent activity model's series entity or freeze a computed expansion that must stay derivable.

findings.name: Schedule change, postponement and cancellation
findings.description: The scheduling status of the occurrence and the authorised transitions that move, postpone, replace or cancel it.

questions.text: What is the current scheduling status of the occurrence, and which statuses are terminal?
Who may postpone, reschedule or cancel this occurrence, and what confirmation does each action require?
How is a counter-proposal of a different time recorded, and how is it resolved?
Which obligations survive a cancellation and which are extinguished by it?
answer_data: Reference to the replacement occurrence where one exists

data_elements.name: Scheduling status
data_elements.description: Coded status of the occurrence, aligned to calendaring and event vocabularies.

data_elements.name: Status changed at
data_elements.description: Instant at which the scheduling status last changed.

data_elements.name: Schedule change reason
data_elements.description: Stated reason for postponement, rescheduling or cancellation.

data_elements.name: Superseding session reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the occurrence that replaces a postponed or rescheduled session.

artifacts.name: Scheduling message
artifacts.description: An exchanged scheduling communication that creates, updates, answers, counter-proposes or cancels the occurrence between the convener and the invited parties.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Message identifier assigned by the sending scheduling agent, always carrying the session identifier, the recurrence instance key where applicable, the revision sequence and the message timestamp used as the tiebreaker when sequences match.

layers.name: Setting, access channel and accessibility
layers.description: The physical venue and resources, the virtual conferencing endpoints, and the accessibility conditions for equivalent participation.

findings.name: Physical setting and reserved resources
findings.description: Where the occurrence physically takes place, what capacity the setting has, and which rooms, equipment and support services are reserved for it.

questions.text: Where does the session physically take place, and which place record is authoritative for that location?
answer_data: Venue reference to the place model
Coordinates or address as published on the notice

questions.text: Which rooms, equipment and support resources are reserved for the session, and by whom were they reserved?
answer_data: Resource references with resource type codes

questions.text: What is the capacity of the setting, and how is over-subscription handled?

data_elements.name: Venue reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the authoritative place record for the physical setting.

data_elements.name: Room designation
data_elements.description: Local designation of the room or space within the venue.

data_elements.name: Venue coordinates
data_elements.description: Point geometry for the setting where published.

data_elements.name: Reserved resource
data_elements.description: Rooms, equipment and services reserved for the occurrence with their resource type codes.

data_elements.name: Attendee capacity
data_elements.description: Maximum number of attendees the setting or session admits.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Venue and resource master records are owned by place and asset models; this finding carries references, a local designation and capacity numbers. A booking confirmation belongs to the reservation system, not to the semantics of the session.

findings.name: Virtual access channel and mixed-mode equivalence
findings.description: The conferencing endpoints published for the session, the admission control applied to them, and what guarantees equivalent participation across modes.

questions.text: Which conferencing endpoints are published for this session, and what features does each provide?
answer_data: Feature codes (audio, video, chat, screen, phone, moderator)

answer_data: Reference to the secret store holding the moderator code
Distribution rule for participant access codes

questions.text: How is admission to the virtual room controlled before and during the session?
answer_data: Admission policy code (anonymous, authenticated, closed list)

questions.text: In a mixed-mode session, what guarantees that remote and in-room participants have equivalent standing?

data_elements.name: Conference endpoint
data_elements.description: Published access point for the conferencing system serving the occurrence.

data_elements.name: Endpoint feature code
data_elements.description: Governed feature codes describing what an endpoint supports.

data_elements.name: Admission control mode
data_elements.description: Policy governing who may join the virtual room.

data_elements.name: Moderator secret reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the externally held moderator access code; the value itself is never stored here.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Endpoints and admission modes are reference data, and access codes must remain in an external secret store rather than being materialised as an artifact of the session. Conference state and floor mechanics are the platform's runtime concern, not a document this model issues.

data_elements.description: Instant at which accessible materials were circulated.

data_elements.name: Caption quality note
data_elements.description: Assessment note on live caption or interpretation quality for this occurrence.

artifacts.name: Accessibility accommodation request
artifacts.description: The captured request for an accessibility accommodation for this occurrence, together with the disposition given to it.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Request identifier issued by the capturing service desk or registration system, bound to the session identifier and the requesting party reference; where no such system exists a Dimension-assigned ULID is used.

bundles.name: Participation, presence and quorum
bundles.description: Who was invited, in what capacity, who actually took part, and whether the occurrence was competent to transact business.
bundles.rationale: Calendaring standards define invitation roles and response states normatively; conferencing platforms produce observed presence data; company law and open-meeting law attach validity to quorum and to the recorded list of persons present. These are distinct facts and must not be conflated.

layers.name: Roles, invitation state and substitution
layers.description: The invited population, the capacity each party holds, and the mechanisms by which participation can be transferred or withdrawn.

findings.name: Participant roles and invitation state
findings.description: The capacity in which each invited party is expected to take part, and the current state of their response to the invitation.

questions.text: Which role does each invited party hold in this occurrence, and which roles must be filled for it to proceed?
answer_data: Role code per invitee (chair, required participant, optional participant, non-participant, secretary)
Mandatory role set for this meeting type
Vacancy indication where a mandatory role is unfilled

questions.text: What invitation response has each invited party given, and when was that response last updated?
Which invited entries denote individuals, which denote groups, and which denote rooms or other resources?
answer_data: Group membership reference where the entry stands for a group

questions.text: Is a response expected from each invitee, and what is assumed when none is given by the session start?
answer_data: Effect of a non-response on quorum counting

data_elements.name: Invitee reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the party model entry for an invited person, group or resource.

data_elements.name: Participant role code
data_elements.description: Governed role code describing the capacity of the invitee at this occurrence.

data_elements.name: Participation status code
data_elements.description: Governed response state of the invitee to the invitation.

data_elements.name: Participant kind code
data_elements.description: Whether the invited entry is an individual, group, room or other resource.

data_elements.name: Response updated at
data_elements.description: Instant at which the participation status was last changed by the invitee.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Invitation state is a per-party tuple of role, status and instant held on the occurrence, and the parties themselves are mastered elsewhere. The document that carries these values outward is the scheduling message already declared under schedule change, so no additional artifact is warranted.

findings.name: Delegation, proxy and recusal
findings.description: Transfer of participation to another party, the rights that transfer with it, and the withdrawal of a participant from part of the proceedings.

questions.text: May an invitee delegate participation, and to whom was participation delegated for this occurrence?
Does a delegate or alternate inherit the delegator's speaking and voting rights in full?
answer_data: Instrument that fixes the transfer rule

questions.text: How is a proxy or voting instruction recorded, and when does it lapse?
Which declared interests require a participant to withdraw from part of the proceedings, and over which items?
answer_data: Withdrawal interval and whether the participant was counted for quorum

data_elements.name: Delegation link
data_elements.description: Directed link recording that participation was delegated from one party to another for this occurrence.

data_elements.name: Proxy instruction reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the externally held proxy or voting instruction.

data_elements.name: Substitution scope
data_elements.description: Extent of rights transferred to a delegate or alternate.

data_elements.name: Recusal declaration
data_elements.description: Declared interest and consequent withdrawal from named agenda items.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Delegation and recusal are relationship facts and interval statements scoped to this occurrence. The proxy instrument itself is a governed document owned by the document or company-secretarial model and is referenced rather than reproduced.

layers.name: Presence observation and quorum determination
layers.description: What was actually observed about presence, and the competence determination derived from it against an externally owned threshold.

findings.name: Presence observation
findings.description: Observed presence of parties during the occurrence, the source and reliability of each observation, and reconciliation between competing sources.

questions.text: Who was actually present, and for which intervals of the occurrence was each party present?
answer_data: Join and leave instants per interval

questions.text: Which observation source produced each presence record, and how reliable is that source?
answer_data: Observation source code (roll call, signed sheet, platform telemetry)
Observation or ingestion instant distinct from the event instant

questions.text: How is presence reconciled when in-room and platform-derived observations disagree?
answer_data: Corrected value and who authorised the correction

questions.text: For how long does platform-derived presence data remain retrievable before it expires at source?
answer_data: Reference to the exported copy once taken

artifacts.name: Attendance register
artifacts.description: The list of persons recorded as present at the occurrence, in the form required by the applicable regime.
media_or_form: attendance list annexed to the record
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the session identifier plus a register sequence within the occurrence; where a secretariat register system exists, its register entry identifier is authoritative.

artifacts.name: Platform attendance report
artifacts.description: Exported attendance observation produced by the conferencing platform, containing per-participant join and leave intervals and totals.
artifacts.identity_strategy: The platform's report identifier is authoritative for the exported copy; it is bound to the session identifier and to the platform conference object identifier, and the export instant is recorded separately from the meeting instants.

findings.name: Quorum determination
findings.description: The determination, at this occurrence, of whether the number and composition of those present met the threshold required to transact business.

questions.text: Which quorum rule applies to this occurrence, and which instrument defines the threshold?
answer_data: Reference to the quorum rule owned by the convening body
Threshold expression as resolved at the occurrence
Composition conditions beyond a bare count

questions.text: Was the quorum satisfied at the opening and at each point where business was decided?
answer_data: Satisfied or not-satisfied outcome per check

questions.text: What is the effect on business transacted if the quorum is lost part-way through the occurrence?
answer_data: Consequence applied (suspension, adjournment, invalidation of the item)

questions.text: Who verifies the quorum, and on whose request must a verification be carried out?
answer_data: Minimum requesting number where a request is required

data_elements.name: Quorum rule reference

data_elements.name: Quorum threshold value
data_elements.description: Threshold as resolved for this occurrence, expressed as a count or proportion.

data_elements.name: Quorum check

data_elements.name: Quorum satisfied flag
data_elements.description: Outcome of the most recent quorum determination.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The threshold rule is owned by the convening body model and is only referenced here; what is local is a small series of determinations with instants, counts and outcomes. Publishing these as an artifact would pre-empt the minutes, which is the record that carries them outward.

bundles.name: Agenda and conduct of proceedings
bundles.description: The business set down for the occurrence, the procedural acts by which it was handled, and the deliberative outcomes reached.
bundles.rationale: Agenda structure, procedural acts, speech attribution and voting are the substance of a session and have an explicit, standardised vocabulary in parliamentary and legal document standards. They are conduct facts of the occurrence, distinct from the durable records that later report them.

layers.name: Agenda composition and control
layers.description: How the business is structured before the session and how it is altered once the session has opened.

findings.name: Agenda item structure
findings.description: The items of business set down for the occurrence, their ordering, purpose, sponsorship, supporting papers and time allocation.

questions.text: Which supporting papers are tabled for each item, and from where do they resolve?

questions.text: How much time is allocated to each item, and what happens when the allocation is exceeded?

layers.name: Procedural acts and floor management
layers.description: The sequence of procedural acts during the occurrence and the allocation of the right to speak.

answer_data: Challenge to the declaration where raised

answer_data: Appeal outcome where the ruling was challenged

Reconstruction note with its author reference

findings.inline_only_rationale: Procedural acts are an ordered set of typed events on the occurrence, and the outward-facing document that reports them is the minutes, owned by WM-REC-012. Declaring an artifact here would create a parallel narrative record competing with the durable one.

findings.name: Floor and speaking management

Addressee where the contribution is directed

answer_data: Limit per speaker or per group

artifacts.name: Speakers list

media_or_form: speakers list maintained by the chair or clerk
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the session identifier plus the agenda item reference under which the list was maintained; where a floor-control system produces the queue, its queue identifier is recorded as a bound external identifier.

layers.name: Motions, voting and outcomes
layers.description: Questions put to the occurrence, the method by which they were decided, and the follow-up that flows from them.

findings.name: Motion and vote conduct
findings.description: How a question is put, by which method it is decided, what tally results and who declares the outcome — the conduct of deciding, not the durable decision itself.

answer_data: Motion or question text as put
Amendments taken before the substantive question

Threshold expression (simple majority, qualified majority, unanimity)
Basis on which the threshold is calculated

answer_data: Votes in favour, against and abstaining
Individual votes where the method is recorded
Declaring officer reference and declaration instant

How is a tied or failed vote resolved at this occurrence?
answer_data: Recorded outcome where the question falls

findings.name: Outcomes and follow-up assignment

answer_data: Routing flag indicating a decision record is owed
Reference to the decision record once created

answer_data: Due date and the task record reference where one is opened

artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the session identifier plus an action ordinal within the occurrence; once a task record is opened, the task model's identifier becomes authoritative for that action and is recorded as a bound reference.

bundles.name: In-session capture and record obligation
bundles.description: What was captured while the occurrence ran, on what basis, and which durable records the occurrence owes to whom.
bundles.rationale: Capture during a session and the durable record produced from it are different things with different owners. Open-meeting and company-law regimes impose specific obligations to produce and certify records, while capture itself raises notification and consent duties at the moment it happens.

layers.name: Capture and record hand-off
layers.description: Recording and live transcription performed during the occurrence, and the obligation to produce durable records from it.

findings.name: Recording and transcription capture

questions.text: Which capture media were produced, and where are they held pending disposition?
answer_data: Duration and integrity evidence per object

questions.text: What happens to captured media if a participant withdraws consent after the occurrence?
answer_data: Remediation applied (redaction request, restriction, disposal request)
Reference to the policy owner that executes the remediation

Legal or policy basis per record type

Content elements that may be withheld

How is the produced record linked back to this occurrence and to individual agenda items and procedural acts?
answer_data: Anchor map from record passages to item and act identifiers

findings.inline_only_rationale: The minutes, transcript and decision records are owned by WM-REC-012 and WM-REC-010; declaring them as artifacts here would duplicate their identity, approval and disposition lifecycle. What is local is the obligation statement, the producer and certifier references, and the anchor map, all of which are reference data on the occurrence.

bundles.name: Confidentiality, admission and interchange
bundles.description: How open the occurrence is, what personal data it holds, and how it is projected into external vocabularies and platforms.
bundles.rationale: Openness classification and closure procedure are governed by statute in public-body settings, and session context concentrates personal data about attendance and contributions. Interchange is a separate, purely declarative concern that keeps the model independent of any storage format or platform.

layers.name: Openness, admission and personal data
layers.description: The openness determination and its procedure, who may be admitted to observe, and the personal data the occurrence holds about participants.

Default applied where no explicit determination was made

Instant at which closure took effect

answer_data: Embargo expression and its end instant
