model.name: Decision / Approval Record
model.purpose: Provide the format-neutral context an agent needs to identify, create, interpret, validate and operate an authoritative record of a decision or approval: what was decided, on what question, by whom under what authority, on what reasons and evidence, with what conditions, from when until when it is valid, and how it is superseded, challenged, disclosed and retained.
model.scope_statement: The model covers the record that constitutes or evidences a discrete decision or approval act and the act's decision-relevant attributes. It treats the decision act and the record of it as distinct but co-modelled: the act supplies authority, outcome, reasons and timing; the record supplies identity, versioned expression, integrity evidence, disclosure and disposition. It spans administrative decisions, judicial judgments, corporate and board resolutions, delegated sign-offs, gate/change approvals and retained machine authorization decisions. It excludes the deliberative occasion, the containing case or procedure, the norms applied, party master data and generic record custody mechanics, which belong to sibling or parent models.
in_scope: Decision identity, versioned expression identity and classification of decision or approval type
Decided question, outcome/disposition, attached conditions, obligations and advice
Statement of reasons, alternatives considered and rejected, evidence and findings of fact relied on
Decision authority, legal or constitutional basis, delegation, approval limits, quorum and voting
Approval participation acts, dissent, abstention, recusal and conflict-of-interest declarations
Attestation evidence: signature, seal, trusted time-stamp token, hash and finality of the record
Distinct decision-relevant times: taken, consented, issued, served, published, in force, recorded
Validity window, retroactivity, conditions of validity, expiry and renewal
Status model, finality, supersession, amendment, corrigendum, revocation and annulment
Challenge, appeal, review outcome and suspensive effect
Automated, assisted and solely automated decision modes with human oversight and contestability
Publication, individual notification/service, access classification, redaction and anonymisation
Decision-specific retention triggers, disposition and disposal/legal hold
Alignment to external decision identifiers and vocabularies (ECLI, Akoma Ntoso, PROV, DCMI, XACML)
out_of_scope: The deliberative occasion itself — agenda, attendance, minutes as a whole (WM-ACT-025 Meeting)
The containing administrative case, application or procedure lifecycle (WM-POL-017)
Generic record custody, storage media, format migration and preservation mechanics (parent WM-REC-001)
The normative content of the policy, statute, rule or standard being applied (policy/rule sibling model)
Master data for persons, organisational units and positions holding decision roles (party/agent sibling model)
Authoring and administration of machine access-control policies; only a retained decision result is in scope
Contract or agreement terms that a decision may authorise (agreement sibling model)
Workflow engine internals, task queues and routing logic that carry an approval request
Downstream financial posting, permit issuance or benefit payment produced by a decision

boundary_notes.distinction: A meeting is an occasion; a decision record is an outcome assertion. The relationship is optional in both directions: Delaware General Corporation Law §141(f) permits board action without any meeting by unanimous written or electronic consent, and delegated single-signature approvals never involve a meeting. Meeting attendance and agenda stay in the meeting model; only the linkage, the agenda item decided and the quorum/vote result attach to the decision record.

A case is the procedural container and may hold many decisions — procedural, interim, partial and final. Case state transitions are driven by decisions but are not decisions. Ex parte communications belong to the case record and are referenced by the decision record only where a rule requires them to be placed on the record of decision.

The parent supplies generic record properties: authenticity, reliability, integrity and usability as record characteristics, custody, format and preservation. WM-REC-010 adds only what is decision-specific — authority, outcome, reasons, validity and supersession — and must not restate parent mechanics.

A PDP result has the same logical shape (decision value, status, obligations, advice, applicable policy identifiers) but is normally ephemeral and produced at log scale. The boundary is retention as a record: a PDP result becomes an instance of this model only when it is captured and managed as a record. XACML decision values are an alignment vocabulary, not the canonical outcome set.

A judgment is a specialised decision record with a governed global identifier (ECLI) and a document structure of introduction, background, motivation and decision. That structure is judicial and must not be imposed on administrative or corporate decisions; court organisation, procedure and case-law citation networks are out of scope.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Electronic signature, seal and time-stamp evidence
boundary_notes.distinction: Attestation evidence is referenced, not owned. The decision record holds pointers to signature/seal objects and time-stamp tokens plus a verification verdict and verification time; the cryptographic object model, trust lists and long-term validation data belong to a signature-evidence sibling model.

Boundary under review. In this model an approval is either an outcome value of a decision or a participation act within one, because the cited sources give approvals no independent identity. Standing authorisations such as licences and permits do have independent validity and holders, and may justify a separate sibling model; flagged rather than assumed.

ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022 treats an architecture decision as pertaining to concerns and affecting architecture description elements, with rationale covering alternatives not chosen. That is a design-governance specialisation of the same shape; the architecture description, viewpoints and models it affects are out of scope here.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Normative model for attributing a decision activity to responsible agents (wasAssociatedWith), qualifying that association with a role and a plan (Association, hadRole, hadPlan), representing delegation (actedOnBehalfOf), derivation of a superseding decision (wasDerivedFrom), invalidation (wasInvalidatedBy) and separate activity/entity times.

sources.title: ISO 15489-1:2016 Information and documentation — Records management — Part 1: Concepts and principles
sources.relevance: Defines records as evidence of business activity, the four characteristics that make a record authoritative (authenticity, reliability, integrity, usability), records metadata, appraisal, records controls and records processes. Anchors why a decision record must be fixed, attributable and disposed under authority. Full normative text is paywalled; iso.org returned HTTP 403 to automated retrieval, so claims are catalogue/abstract level.

sources.title: eXtensible Access Control Markup Language (XACML) Version 3.0
sources.relevance: Normative four-valued decision vocabulary (Permit, Deny, NotApplicable, Indeterminate), the Result structure (Decision, Status, Obligations, AssociatedAdvice, PolicyIdentifierList), the binding distinction between obligations that must be discharged and advice that may be ignored, and the PDP/PEP/PAP/PIP role separation for machine-rendered decisions.

sources.title: 5 U.S.C. § 557 — Initial decisions; conclusiveness; review by agency; submissions by parties; contents of decisions; record
sources.relevance: Requires the record of a decision to show findings, conclusions and the reasons or basis therefor on all material issues of fact, law or discretion, plus the rule, order, sanction, relief or denial; distinguishes initial from agency decisions and recommended decisions by subordinate employees; requires prohibited ex parte communications to be placed on the public record.

sources.title: RFC 3339 — Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Normative timestamp profile: four-digit years, mandatory explicit relationship to UTC via numeric offset or 'Z', the distinct meaning of -00:00 as UTC with unknown local offset, optional fractional seconds and :60 for leap seconds. Governs every time value in this model.

sources.title: European Case Law Identifier (ECLI)
sources.version_or_date: Council conclusions on ECLI, CELEX 52011XG0429(01) (OJ C 127, 29.4.2011)
sources.relevance: Governed global identifier for judicial decisions with five colon-separated components (literal 'ECLI', country code, court code, four-digit year the judgment was rendered, ordinal number up to 25 characters, letters/digits/dots only), plus a recommended Dublin Core-based minimum metadata set. Primary evidence for identity priority and for the rule that a year inside an identifier is not a date field.

sources.title: Article 41 — Right to good administration, Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union
sources.organization: European Union Agency for Fundamental Rights (FRA)
sources.relevance: Establishes the obligation of the administration to give reasons for its decisions (41(2)(c)), the right to be heard before an adverse individual measure (41(2)(a)) and the right of access to one's own file subject to confidentiality and business secrecy (41(2)(b)). Grounds the reasons, hearing and party-access findings.

sources.title: DCMI Metadata Terms
sources.relevance: Supplies distinct governed properties this model needs to keep separate: valid (date or range of validity), issued (formal issuance), created, modified, dateAccepted, replaces / isReplacedBy for supersession, provenance for custody changes, accessRights, rightsHolder, conformsTo and identifier. Also the metadata family ECLI recommends.

sources.title: Akoma Ntoso Version 1.0. Part 1: XML Vocabulary
sources.relevance: FRBR-based four-level identity for legal documents (Work, Expression, Manifestation, Item) expressed as IRIs, and the judgment document structure of introduction, background, motivation and decision. Primary support for separating the decision as an abstract work from its language versions, corrected versions and published formats.

sources.title: Delaware General Corporation Law, Title 8, Chapter 1, Subchapter IV — Directors and Officers (§ 141)
sources.version_or_date: Delaware Code, current through the 2025 legislative session
sources.relevance: Primary counterexample source for decision mechanics: quorum defaults and floors (§141(b), never less than one third), committee powers and their express limits (§141(c)), remote participation counting as presence in person (§141(i)), and action without a meeting by unanimous written or electronic consent filed with the minutes, optionally conditioned to take effect up to 60 days later (§141(f)).

sources.title: Universal Electronic Records Management (ERM) Requirements
sources.organization: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)
sources.relevance: Lifecycle requirement groups (capture, maintenance and use, disposal, transfer, metadata, reporting) with Must Have / Should Have grading, and the program-versus-system requirement split. Grounds capture, disposition, transfer and metadata findings without importing a single national retention schedule.

sources.title: RFC 3161 — Internet X.509 Public Key Infrastructure Time-Stamp Protocol (TSP)
sources.relevance: Proof-of-existence semantics for attestation: TSTInfo fields version, policy, messageImprint, per-TSA unique serialNumber, genTime, accuracy, ordering, nonce and tsa. Supplies the evidentiary distinction between an asserted signing time and a third-party attested time.

sources.title: AI Act — Regulatory framework for artificial intelligence
sources.organization: European Commission (Directorate-General for Communications Networks, Content and Technology)
sources.version_or_date: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689; in force 1 August 2024, general application from 2 August 2026
sources.relevance: Requires human oversight measures for high-risk AI systems, logging of activity to ensure traceability of results, and provider information duties toward deployers. Grounds the automation, oversight and system-attribution findings. Article-level text was not retrievable from EUR-Lex; obligations are cited at the level this official page states them.

sources.title: Guidelines on Automated individual decision-making and Profiling for the purposes of Regulation 2016/679 (wp251rev.01)
sources.organization: Article 29 Data Protection Working Party (endorsed by the European Data Protection Board)
sources.relevance: Official interpretation of when a decision is 'based solely on automated processing', what counts as legal or similarly significant effects, and what makes human intervention meaningful. Only the item metadata was retrievable at this URL; the substantive guidance sits in the linked PDF and is treated as an interpretive alignment, not a verified quotation.

sources.title: Art. 22 GDPR — Automated individual decision-making, including profiling
sources.relevance: Working text of the right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing producing legal or similarly significant effects, its three exceptions and the minimum safeguards of human intervention, expressing a point of view and contesting the decision. Used because EUR-Lex was not retrievable; must be re-verified against the Official Journal before any conformance claim.

sources.title: ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010:2022 Software, systems and enterprise — Architecture description
sources.relevance: Normative treatment of architecture decision, architecture rationale, concern and stakeholder: a decision pertains to concerns and affects description elements, and rationale records justification including alternatives not chosen. Supports the reasons and options-considered findings as a general decision pattern. Full text paywalled; iso.org returned HTTP 403 to automated retrieval.

sources.title: MoReq2010: Modular Requirements for Records Systems — Volume 1: Core Services & Plug-in Modules
sources.version_or_date: MoReq2010, published 2011 (no further development pursued after 2018)
sources.relevance: Modular records-system requirement set built on core services with an explicit entity model covering records, aggregations, classes, disposal scheduling, disposal holding and an immutable event history. Supports the finality, event-history and hold findings. Development is discontinued, so it is treated as a stable reference rather than an evolving obligation.

sources.title: ISO 23081 Metadata for records (ISO 23081-1:2017 principles; ISO 23081-2:2021 conceptual and implementation issues)
sources.relevance: Primary statement that records metadata must support integrity, authenticity, reliability and usability, and must tell who did what to which digital object across the record's life.

sources.title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
sources.relevance: Domain-agnostic provenance for the decision record as an entity: generation and invalidation times, usage of input entities, attribution and association of agents, delegation (actedOnBehalfOf), identifiers and derivation/revision.

sources.title: Decision Model and Notation (DMN) Specification Version 1.5
sources.relevance: Defines precise, often executable specification of repeatable business decisions. Used as an alignment boundary: DMN is decision logic, not the authorised instance record with approver and validity.

sources.title: 5 U.S.C. § 557 Initial decisions; conclusiveness; review by agency; submissions by parties; contents of decisions; record
sources.organization: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration (Office of the Federal Register)
sources.version_or_date: Administrative Procedure Act; page last reviewed 2016-08-15
sources.relevance: Normative contents of an adjudicative decision record: findings, conclusions and reasons on material issues; the rule, order, sanction, relief or denial; initial, recommended and tentative grades; appeal and agency review; inclusion of all such decisions in the record; ex parte communication rules and docketing.

sources.title: Markdown Architectural Decision Records (MADR)
sources.relevance: Operational template for any important decision record: status vocabulary (proposed, rejected, accepted, deprecated, superseded), decision-makers, consulted and informed roles, context, drivers, options, outcome, consequences and confirmation.

sources.title: Documenting Architecture Decisions
sources.relevance: Canonical lightweight ADR: one decision per record; sequential identifiers not reused; Context, Decision, Status and Consequences; proposed/accepted/deprecated/superseded; keep superseded records rather than deleting them.

sources.title: ISO 15489 (DCC Standards Watch briefing)
sources.relevance: Secondary exposition of record characteristics and the capture–registration–classification–access–disposition process chain. Used only to surface process detail; version predates ISO 15489-1:2016.

bundles.name: Identity and classification
bundles.description: How a decision or approval record is uniquely designated, versioned as expressions and manifestations, typed, and bounded in subject matter and applicability.
bundles.rationale: An agent cannot cite, deduplicate, supersede or retrieve a decision without a stable identity separated from its versions, and cannot apply the right rules without knowing the decision type and its scope of effect. ECLI proves that decision identity is a governed concern in its own right, and Akoma Ntoso proves that the decision as a work differs from its language and format versions.

layers.name: Identity and designation
layers.description: Identifier assignment for the decision act and its record, and the versioned expression structure that keeps corrections and translations distinct from the abstract decision.

findings.name: Decision and record identifier assignment
findings.description: The identifier that designates the decision, the authority that mints it, and the separation between the identifier of the decision act, the identifier of the record and any governed global identifier such as an ECLI.

questions.text: Which identifier scheme designates this decision, and which body governs and issues values in that scheme?
Does the identifier designate the decision act, the record documenting it, or both, and how is the other one identified?
answer_data: Companion identifier for the other referent

questions.text: When an authoritative master-system number, a governed global identifier and a locally minted UUID/ULID all exist, which is canonical for citation and which are aliases?
answer_data: Ordered list of alias identifiers with scheme and issuer

questions.text: How is an identifier minted for a decision taken without a meeting, a case number or a hearing — for example a delegated sign-off or unanimous written consent?
answer_data: Whether the identifier is sequential within a series

questions.text: Are any date-bearing tokens inside the identifier being relied on as the decision date, and if so how is that dependency removed?
answer_data: Explicit statement that embedded years are not date fields
Pointer to the authoritative date element

data_elements.name: canonical_decision_identifier
data_elements.description: The single canonical identifier used to cite this decision, expressed with its scheme.

data_elements.name: identifier_scheme
data_elements.description: Governing scheme of the canonical identifier, for example an ECLI, a national register number or an internal case-management series.

data_elements.name: alias_identifiers
data_elements.description: Other identifiers denoting the same decision or its record, each with scheme, issuer and referent type.

data_elements.name: record_identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the record object when it differs from the identifier of the decision act.

artifacts.name: Identifier register entry
artifacts.description: The register or minting-log entry that evidences assignment of the canonical identifier to this decision, including issuer, series and assignment time.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the register's own entry number issued by the minting authority; where the register is an ECLI coordinator's register, the ECLI itself is the entry key.

findings.name: Version, expression and manifestation identity
findings.description: How successive language versions, corrected texts, consolidated texts and published formats of the same decision are distinguished without fragmenting its identity.

questions.text: At which identity level does each stored item sit — abstract decision (work), a specific version or language (expression), a format (manifestation), or a single file (item)?
Which expression is the authentic or authoritative text, and what governs divergence between language versions?
When a text is corrected, is a new expression created or is the existing one edited, and how is the superseded expression preserved?
Does an anonymised or redacted published expression exist alongside a full internal expression, and are they explicitly linked?

data_elements.name: work_identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the abstract decision independent of version, language and format.

data_elements.name: expression_descriptor
data_elements.description: Language, version label and version date that discriminate one expression of the decision from another.

data_elements.name: is_authentic_expression
data_elements.description: Whether this expression is the authoritative text for legal or evidential purposes.

data_elements.name: manifestation_format
data_elements.description: Concrete format in which an expression is rendered, for example a signed PDF/A file, an XML instance or a paper original.

artifacts.name: Consolidated or corrected text
artifacts.description: A distinct expression of the decision incorporating corrigenda or amendments, carrying its own expression identifier and a reference to the expressions it replaces.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Work identifier plus expression discriminator (language and version date), following the FRBR-based IRI convention; never re-uses the identifier of the expression it replaces.

findings.name: Title, language and alternative names
findings.description: A short noun-phrase title representing the problem and chosen solution, plus language and any alternative citations. DCMI title and alternative apply; Nygard and MADR require a short representative heading.

questions.text: What short title names this decision in terms of the problem solved and the outcome chosen?
In which language or languages is the authoritative text of the decision expressed?
What alternative names, docket numbers or popular citations should retrieve the same record without becoming identifiers?

data_elements.name: Title
data_elements.description: Short noun-phrase heading for the decision record.

data_elements.name: Primary language
data_elements.description: Language tag of the authoritative decision text.

data_elements.name: Alternative titles or citations
data_elements.description: Other human labels that refer to the same record.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Title and language are intrinsic descriptive metadata of the record, not a standalone artefact.

layers.name: Classification and subject matter
layers.description: The type of decision or approval, its binding character, and the subject matter, jurisdiction and population to which it applies.

findings.name: Decision type and binding character
findings.description: Classification of the record along the axes that change how it must be handled: decision family, binding versus advisory, interim versus final, and positive versus negative outcome.

questions.text: Which decision family does this record belong to — administrative decision, judicial judgment, corporate resolution, delegated approval, gate or change approval, or retained machine authorization decision?
Is the instrument binding, or is it an opinion, recommendation or advice that does not itself dispose of the matter?
Is this an interim, partial, recommended or final decision, and if not final what does it leave undecided?
answer_data: Reference to the anticipated final decision

questions.text: Where an external decision vocabulary is used, is it the canonical classification or an alignment, and what does not map?

data_elements.name: decision_family
data_elements.description: Coded decision family that selects the applicable handling, authority and retention rules.

data_elements.name: binding_character
data_elements.description: Whether the instrument is binding, advisory or recommendatory.

data_elements.name: procedural_stage
data_elements.description: Interim, partial, recommended or final position of this decision in its procedure.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Classification is a set of coded attributes of the decision record itself. It produces no separate deliverable object; the controlled vocabularies it draws on are governed by the Dimension's registry links rather than by an artifact of this finding.

findings.name: Subject matter and scope of application
findings.description: What the decision is about and how far its effect reaches — addressees only or a general class, which territory or jurisdiction, and which organisational or asset scope.

questions.text: What subject matter does the decision concern, and against which classification scheme is that subject expressed?
Does the decision bind only named addressees, or does it apply generally to a class of persons, cases or objects?
Which jurisdiction, territory or organisational unit does the decision operate in, and is its effect limited to that boundary?
answer_data: Statement of extraterritorial effect if any

questions.text: Is the decision intended to have precedential or policy effect beyond the instant matter, and who may rely on it?
answer_data: Publication requirement triggered by precedential status

data_elements.name: subject_descriptors
data_elements.description: Coded or textual descriptors of the matter decided.

data_elements.name: scope_of_effect
data_elements.description: Whether the decision has individual effect on named addressees or general effect on a defined class.

data_elements.name: jurisdiction
data_elements.description: Jurisdiction or organisational domain within which the decision operates.

data_elements.name: territorial_extent
data_elements.description: Geographic extent of effect where the decision is territorially bounded.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Subject and scope are inline descriptive attributes and references to externally governed classification schemes and jurisdiction registers. Producing a separate artifact would duplicate those registers, which belong to sibling classification models.

bundles.name: Substance and reasoning
bundles.description: The decided question, the outcome and any attached conditions or obligations, together with the reasons, alternatives considered and evidence that support the outcome.
bundles.rationale: Substance and reasons are the part of a decision record that authorities most often make mandatory: 5 U.S.C. §557(c) requires findings, conclusions and reasons on all material issues, Charter Article 41(2)(c) imposes a duty to give reasons, and ISO/IEC/IEEE 42010 requires rationale that covers alternatives not chosen. Outcome vocabularies and the obligation/advice split are given normative shape by XACML.

layers.name: Decision substance
layers.description: The question put, the disposition reached, and the conditions, obligations and implementation duties attached to it.

findings.name: Question put for decision
findings.description: The precise question, proposal, motion or request the decision resolves, including how it was framed and by whom it was brought.

questions.text: What exact question, motion or proposal was put, and in what wording was it put to the deciding body?
What triggered the decision — an application, a referral, a statutory duty, a scheduled review or an own-initiative act — and who initiated it?
answer_data: Reference to the triggering request or instrument

questions.text: Which stakeholder concerns, requirements or criteria was the decision required to address?
answer_data: Mapping from concerns to the outcome

questions.text: Was the question amended, split or reframed before decision, and is the final wording distinguishable from the original?

data_elements.name: question_text
data_elements.description: Verbatim wording of the question, motion or proposal decided.

data_elements.name: trigger_reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the application, referral, duty or scheduled review that caused the decision to be taken.

data_elements.name: addressed_concerns
data_elements.description: Concerns, criteria or requirements the decision was required to resolve.

artifacts.name: Proposal, motion or application as submitted
artifacts.description: The originating document that put the question — an application form, a submitted motion, a board paper or a referral — as received, before amendment.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the submitting or receiving system's authoritative intake reference; falls back to a Dimension-assigned ULID when the submission arrived without a governed reference.

findings.name: Outcome and disposition
findings.description: The operative determination: the outcome value, the order or relief granted or refused, and any non-outcome such as deferral, withdrawal or inability to decide.

questions.text: What is the operative outcome value, and from which controlled vocabulary is it drawn?
How are non-dispositive results represented — deferral, adjournment, withdrawal, no quorum, tie, not applicable or unable to determine?
Which part of the record is the operative determination, and which parts are reasoning that does not bind?
Where the decision grants in part and refuses in part, how is each element of relief and refusal separately expressed?
answer_data: Itemised relief elements with per-item outcome

questions.text: If an external four-valued authorization vocabulary is used, which administrative outcomes have no equivalent and how is that recorded?
answer_data: Mapping table to external decision values

data_elements.name: outcome_code
data_elements.description: Coded operative outcome, for example granted, refused, granted with conditions, deferred, withdrawn, no decision or indeterminate.

data_elements.name: operative_text
data_elements.description: Verbatim operative part stating the rule, order, sanction, relief or denial.

data_elements.name: outcome_items
data_elements.description: Per-item outcomes where the decision disposes of several requests or heads of relief separately.

data_elements.name: outcome_status_detail
data_elements.description: Machine status detail explaining an indeterminate or not-applicable result, such as a missing attribute or an evaluation error.

artifacts.name: Signed decision instrument
artifacts.description: The issued instrument that carries the operative determination — the order, judgment, resolution, permit decision or notice of refusal — in its authentic expression.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Bears the canonical decision identifier from the issuing authority's decision series; where the authority participates in a governed global scheme the scheme identifier is carried on the face of the instrument.

findings.name: Conditions, obligations, advice and implementation duties
findings.description: What must happen for the decision to take or keep effect, what the decision obliges parties to do, what is merely advisory, and which implementation and enforcement duties follow.

questions.text: Which conditions must be satisfied before the decision takes effect, and which conditions if breached end its effect?
answer_data: Condition precedent list with due dates
Condition subsequent list with breach consequences

questions.text: Which attached requirements are binding obligations that must be discharged and which are advice that may be disregarded without invalidating the outcome?
answer_data: Obligation list with obligor and deadline
Rule for handling an obligation that cannot be discharged

questions.text: Who is responsible for implementing and enforcing the decision, and what happens if it is not implemented?
Is effectiveness deliberately deferred to a later date or a future event, and is there a maximum permitted deferral?
answer_data: Deferred effective date as RFC 3339 timestamp
Maximum deferral rule and its source

data_elements.name: conditions
data_elements.description: Conditions precedent and subsequent with type, due date, verifying party and current satisfaction state.

data_elements.name: obligations
data_elements.description: Binding obligations attached to the outcome, each with obligor, description and discharge deadline.

data_elements.name: advisory_items
data_elements.description: Non-binding advice attached to the outcome that may be disregarded without affecting validity.

data_elements.name: implementing_party
data_elements.description: Party accountable for carrying the decision into effect.

artifacts.name: Condition compliance evidence
artifacts.description: Evidence lodged to show that a condition precedent or subsequent has been satisfied, such as a certificate, inspection report or payment confirmation.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the issuing body's own certificate or report number; otherwise a Dimension-assigned ULID linked to the condition identifier it discharges.

layers.name: Reasoning and evidence
layers.description: The stated reasons, the alternatives weighed and rejected, and the evidence and findings of fact on which the outcome rests.

findings.name: Statement of reasons
findings.description: The reasoning that justifies the outcome, whether giving reasons is legally required for this decision, and whether the reasons form part of the operative instrument or a separate document.

questions.text: Is there a legal or policy duty to give reasons for this decision, and what instrument imposes it?
answer_data: Consequence of failing to give reasons

questions.text: Do the reasons address all material issues of fact, law and discretion presented, and how is that completeness checked?
answer_data: Issue list with per-issue reasoning reference

questions.text: Are the reasons part of the operative instrument, an annexed statement, or a separately requestable document?
answer_data: Rule on requesting reasons after the fact

questions.text: Where reasons are abbreviated, standardised or omitted, what justifies that and is a fuller statement available on request?
answer_data: Availability of full reasons and how to obtain them

data_elements.name: reasons_text
data_elements.description: The statement of findings, conclusions and the reasons or basis for them on the material issues.

data_elements.name: reasons_duty_basis
data_elements.description: Instrument and provision imposing the duty to give reasons, where one applies.

data_elements.name: issue_to_reason_map
data_elements.description: Mapping from each material issue raised to the passage of reasoning that resolves it.

artifacts.name: Statement of reasons document
artifacts.description: The document setting out findings, conclusions and reasons, whether embodied in the decision instrument or issued as a separate annexed or later-requested statement.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Inherits the decision's work identifier with a part or annex discriminator when embodied in the instrument; carries its own issuing reference when produced separately after request.

findings.name: Options considered and rejected
findings.description: The alternatives evaluated, the criteria and weights applied, and the recorded justification for rejecting each alternative not chosen.

questions.text: Which alternatives were formally considered, and is the list complete relative to what the deciding body was given?
Against which criteria and weights were the alternatives assessed, and were those criteria fixed before assessment?
For each rejected alternative, what is the recorded reason for rejection?
Was the status quo or 'take no action' option explicitly assessed, and on what basis was it set aside?

data_elements.name: considered_options
data_elements.description: Alternatives assessed, each with description, assessment result and rejection reason where not chosen.

data_elements.name: assessment_criteria
data_elements.description: Criteria and weights used to compare alternatives.

data_elements.name: option_scores
data_elements.description: Recorded scores or comparative assessments per option and criterion.

artifacts.name: Options appraisal or comparative analysis
artifacts.description: The analysis put before the deciding body comparing alternatives against criteria, including any scoring model and its assumptions.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the authoring body's document reference; linked to the decision by the decision's canonical identifier plus a role qualifier marking it as an input relied upon.

findings.name: Evidence relied upon and findings of fact
findings.description: The inputs the decision-maker used, the facts found from them, submissions received, and any communications that a rule requires to be placed on the record.

questions.text: Which specific inputs did the decision-maker use, and are they retained and resolvable at the version actually relied upon?
answer_data: Input references with version or hash

questions.text: What facts were found, and which input supports each finding?
Was the affected party heard before an adverse measure, and what submissions were received and considered?
answer_data: Statement of how submissions were addressed

questions.text: Were any prohibited or off-record communications received, and were they placed on the record as required?
For machine-evaluated inputs, which attribute sources supplied values and were any required attributes missing?
answer_data: Missing attribute list and effect on the outcome

data_elements.name: inputs_used
data_elements.description: References to documents, data and testimony used in reaching the decision, each with a version or content hash.

data_elements.name: findings_of_fact
data_elements.description: Facts found, each linked to its supporting input.

data_elements.name: party_submissions
data_elements.description: Submissions, representations and proposed findings received from parties, with receipt timestamps.

data_elements.name: disclosed_communications
data_elements.description: Communications required to be placed on the record, with content reference and disclosure time.

artifacts.name: Evidence bundle or exhibit list
artifacts.description: The enumerated set of inputs before the decision-maker, fixed at decision time, with per-item references and integrity digests.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the case or matter reference plus a bundle sequence number from the managing system; each entry is keyed by the exhibit number assigned in the procedure.

findings.name: Completeness of rulings and confirmation of implementation
findings.description: APA requires the record to show the ruling on each finding, conclusion or exception. MADR confirmation describes how implementation or compliance will be checked. Completeness is a quality property of the decision record; implementation evidence may live in sibling operational models.

questions.text: Does the record contain a ruling on every material issue and every exception presented, and which items are missing?
How will compliance with the decision be confirmed, and by whom?
Has implementation been confirmed, with what result and evidence?

data_elements.name: Completeness assessment
data_elements.description: Assessment that required rulings are present.

data_elements.name: Confirmation
data_elements.description: Method, due time, status and evidence of implementation or compliance checks.

artifacts.name: Confirmation or compliance evidence
artifacts.description: Review, test, audit or ArchUnit-style check that the chosen decision was implemented.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Child artefact of the decision record or reference to an audit-workpaper sibling.

bundles.name: Authority, approval and attestation
bundles.description: The competence under which the decision was taken, delegation and limits on it, the participation and voting that produced it, declared conflicts, and the evidence that fixes and attributes the record.
bundles.rationale: A decision that exceeds the decider's competence is voidable, so authority is not metadata but a validity condition. Delaware §141 supplies primary rules on quorum, committee limits, remote presence and action without a meeting; 5 U.S.C. §557 separates presiding, recommending and deciding roles; PROV-O supplies the qualified association and delegation pattern; RFC 3161 supplies third-party time attestation.

layers.name: Mandate and competence
layers.description: The source of power to decide, and the delegation instruments and thresholds that bound it.

findings.name: Decision authority and legal basis
findings.description: Which body or role held competence to take this decision, the instrument conferring that competence, and the rules of composition it had to satisfy.

questions.text: Which body, office or role took the decision, as distinct from anyone who prepared, recommended or merely signed it?
Which instrument and provision confer competence to take this decision, and was it in force at the decision time?
answer_data: Version of the instrument relied upon

questions.text: What composition, quorum or qualification rules applied to the deciding body, and what is their source?
answer_data: Composition at the time of decision

questions.text: How is it verified that the decision falls within the conferred competence, and what happens if it does not?

data_elements.name: deciding_authority
data_elements.description: Reference to the body, office or role that took the decision.

data_elements.name: authority_basis
data_elements.description: Instrument and provision conferring competence, with the version relied upon.

data_elements.name: agent_roles
data_elements.description: Qualified roles of each agent associated with the decision activity, for example presiding, recommending, deciding, signing or advising.

data_elements.name: quorum_rule
data_elements.description: Applicable quorum and majority requirement with its source provision.

artifacts.name: Instrument conferring authority
artifacts.description: The statute, charter, bylaw, terms of reference or standing order relied on as the source of competence, at the version in force when the decision was taken.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Referenced by the instrument's own governed identifier and point-in-time version identifier; never copied into the decision record, only cited with the version relied upon.

findings.name: Delegation, sub-delegation and approval limits
findings.description: Where the decision was taken under delegated power, the delegation chain, its thresholds and exclusions, and its validity at the decision time.

questions.text: Who delegated the power, to whom, and is there a sub-delegation chain back to the original holder of competence?
answer_data: Delegator and delegate references in order

questions.text: What monetary, categorical or risk thresholds bound the delegated power, and does this decision fall inside them?
answer_data: Decision value measured against each threshold
Within-limit determination and who made it

questions.text: Which matters are expressly excluded from delegation and reserved to the delegating body?
answer_data: Reserved matter list with source provision

questions.text: Was the delegation in force at the decision time, and had it been revoked, suspended or lapsed?

data_elements.name: delegation_chain
data_elements.description: Ordered chain of delegating and delegated agents with the instrument authorising each step.

data_elements.name: applicable_thresholds
data_elements.description: Thresholds bounding the delegated power and the measured value of this decision against them.

data_elements.name: decision_magnitude
data_elements.description: Quantified magnitude of the decision used to test delegation thresholds, with unit and currency where applicable.

artifacts.name: Delegation of authority instrument
artifacts.description: The signed delegation, authority matrix entry or committee mandate under which the decider acted, at the version in force at decision time.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the issuing organisation's delegation register reference plus a version discriminator; where no register exists, a Dimension-assigned ULID bound to delegator, delegate and effective period.

layers.name: Approval acts, participation and objections
layers.description: The individual acts of approval, participation, voting, dissent and recusal that constitute or evidence the decision.

findings.name: Participation, quorum and vote result
findings.description: Who took part and how, whether quorum was met, how votes or consents were counted, and how decisions taken without a meeting are represented.

questions.text: Was quorum required and met, counted against which denominator, and who determined that?
How were votes cast and counted — in favour, against, abstaining, absent — and what majority did the outcome require?
If the decision was taken without a meeting, how was consent collected, when did it become effective, and where is it filed?
Did any participant attend by remote communication, and does the governing rule count that as presence?
Where approval is multi-step, were the steps sequential or parallel, and was any step skipped, escalated or auto-approved on timeout?
answer_data: Approval step list with order and status
Skip or escalation events with reason

data_elements.name: participants

data_elements.name: vote_tally

data_elements.name: quorum_met
data_elements.description: Whether the applicable quorum requirement was satisfied.

data_elements.name: written_consents
data_elements.description: Individual written or electronic consents where the decision was taken without a meeting, each with consenter and consent timestamp.

artifacts.name: Voting record or unanimous written consent
artifacts.description: The record of votes cast, or the set of individual written or electronic consents constituting action without a meeting, filed alongside the minutes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the governing body's sitting or resolution number and the decision's canonical identifier; individual consents are keyed by consenter identifier plus consent timestamp.

findings.name: Dissent, recusal and conflicts of interest
findings.description: Recorded disagreement with the outcome, withdrawals from participation on interest grounds, and declared conflicts affecting the decision's soundness.

questions.text: Did any participant dissent or issue a separate opinion, and is that text part of the published record?
answer_data: Dissent or separate opinion text reference

questions.text: Did any eligible participant recuse themselves, on what stated ground, and at what point in the process?
What conflicts of interest were declared, by whom, and how were they managed?
answer_data: Declaration entries with declarant and interest description

questions.text: What control detects an undeclared conflict after the decision, and what remedy applies if one is found?

findings.inline_only_rationale: Dissents, recusals and conflict declarations are participation events attached to the decision and are normally captured inline in the decision record or in the meeting minutes owned by WM-ACT-025. Where a dissent is issued as a standalone opinion document it is carried as an additional expression under f02 rather than as an artifact unique to this finding.

layers.name: Attestation and record integrity
layers.description: The evidence that fixes the record's content and attributes it to its signatories, and the point at which it becomes unalterable.

findings.name: Signature, seal, time-stamp and integrity evidence
findings.description: How the record is signed or sealed, how its content is fixed by digest and third-party time attestation, and how a later verifier can re-establish that it has not changed.

questions.text: Who signed or sealed the record, in what capacity, and with what kind of signature or seal?
Is there a third-party attested time of existence for the record content, and how does it differ from the asserted signing time?
Which content was hashed, with which algorithm, and does the digest cover the reasons and annexes as well as the operative part?
When was verification last performed, by whom, with what verdict, and what is the re-verification interval?
answer_data: Re-verification interval and next due date

questions.text: At which lifecycle point does the record become unalterable, and what mechanism enforces that?

data_elements.name: signature_evidence
data_elements.description: References to signature or seal objects with signatory, capacity, type and asserted signing time.

data_elements.name: time_stamp_token
data_elements.description: Third-party time-stamp token reference carrying attested generation time, accuracy, policy and issuer serial number.

data_elements.name: content_digest
data_elements.description: Digest algorithm, value and coverage statement fixing the record content.

data_elements.name: last_verification
data_elements.description: Most recent integrity and attestation verification with verdict, verifier and RFC 3339 verification timestamp.

data_elements.name: fixed_at
data_elements.description: Time at which the record became unalterable, recorded as an RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset or Z.

artifacts.name: Trusted time-stamp token
artifacts.description: A time-stamp token binding a digest of the record to an attested generation time, carrying the issuing authority's per-token serial number, policy identifier and stated accuracy.
media_or_form: archival time-stamp in a long-term signature container
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the issuing authority identifier plus the unique integer serial number that the authority assigns to each token; the token itself is not re-issued or renumbered.

artifacts.name: Immutable event history entry
artifacts.description: Append-only audit entry recording each action taken on the record — capture, approval, issuance, supersession, disposal — with actor, action and time.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Sequential entry number within the record's event history, never reused; each entry additionally carries the record identifier and an RFC 3339 event timestamp.

bundles.name: Time, validity and lifecycle
bundles.description: The distinct times attaching to a decision, the period during which it is valid, its status transitions and finality, and the ways it is superseded, revoked, challenged or annulled.
bundles.rationale: Decision records fail most often on time: a single 'decision date' cannot express that consent became effective when the last consent was delivered, that issuance and service differ, that validity is a range distinct from issuance, or that annulment operates retroactively. RFC 3339, DCMI Terms and Delaware §141(f) each supply primary support for separating these.

layers.name: Temporal frame
layers.description: The set of separately recorded times around a decision, and the validity period distinct from any of them.

findings.name: Decision event timeline
findings.description: The distinct, separately recorded moments in a decision's life — taken, consented, signed, issued, served, published, in force — plus the observation time at which each was recorded.

questions.text: Which distinct times exist for this decision, and which one is the authoritative 'decision time' for citation and for computing deadlines?
Are the time the event occurred and the time it was recorded or ingested stored separately, and how far apart are they?
Does every stored time carry an explicit UTC offset or Z, and how is an unknown local offset represented?
answer_data: Representation used for unknown local offset

questions.text: For action taken by consent rather than at a sitting, what rule fixes the moment the decision was taken?
When was the decision served on or notified to each addressee, and does that start a challenge period?

data_elements.name: decided_at
data_elements.description: Authoritative time the decision was taken, as an RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: issued_at
data_elements.description: Time of formal issuance of the decision instrument.

data_elements.name: recorded_at
data_elements.description: Time the decision was captured into the records system, recorded separately from the event time.

data_elements.name: served_at
data_elements.description: Per-addressee service or notification times that start challenge periods.

data_elements.name: in_force_at
data_elements.description: Time from which the decision produces legal or operational effect, where different from issuance.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The timeline is a set of typed timestamp values on the decision record, each already evidenced by an artifact owned elsewhere in the model: proof of service under f25, the time-stamp token under f15 and the event-history entry under f15. Minting a separate timeline artifact would duplicate those without adding evidential weight.

findings.name: Validity window, retroactivity and expiry
findings.description: The period during which the decision is valid, whether effect reaches backwards in time, and how expiry, renewal and suspension of validity are represented.

questions.text: From when until when is the decision valid, and is the end open, fixed, conditional or event-driven?
answer_data: Validity end timestamp or open-ended marker

questions.text: Does the decision take effect from a date earlier than it was taken, and what authorises that retroactivity?
Can validity be suspended without being ended, and what events suspend and restore it?
answer_data: Suspension events with start and end timestamps

questions.text: Is the decision renewable or subject to periodic review, and does renewal create a new decision or extend this one?
answer_data: Whether renewal mints a new identifier

questions.text: How does a consumer ask whether the decision was valid at a specific past instant, and what does the answer depend on?
answer_data: Inputs required (validity window, suspensions, revocations, annulments)
Returned validity verdict with the instant evaluated

data_elements.name: valid_from
data_elements.description: Start of the period of validity, which may precede the decision time where retroactivity is authorised.

data_elements.name: valid_until
data_elements.description: End of the period of validity, absent where validity is open-ended.

data_elements.name: retroactive_basis
data_elements.description: Provision authorising effect earlier than the decision time, where claimed.

data_elements.name: validity_suspensions
data_elements.description: Suspension intervals during which the decision does not produce effect, each with authority and reason.

data_elements.name: review_due_date
data_elements.description: Date on which the decision falls due for periodic review or renewal.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Validity is a temporal property of the decision expressed inline through a start, an end and suspension intervals. Where an authority issues a separate certificate of validity or currency, that is an outward-facing attestation carried by the notification artifact under f25, not a distinct object owned here.

layers.name: Lifecycle, change and challenge
layers.description: Status transitions and the point of finality, the mechanisms by which a decision is amended, replaced or undone, and the routes by which it can be challenged.

findings.name: Status model and finality
findings.description: The permitted states of a decision record, the transitions between them, and the point at which the decision becomes final and the record unalterable.

questions.text: What is the complete set of permitted states, and which are terminal?
Which transitions are permitted, who may trigger each, and what preconditions guard them?
answer_data: Transition table with source and target states

questions.text: When does the decision become final in the substantive sense — no longer open to ordinary challenge — and is that different from the record becoming unalterable?
At what point does a draft or proposed decision become a record subject to management, and how are pre-record drafts handled?
Which operations remain permitted after finality, and how is each recorded without altering the fixed content?

data_elements.name: status
data_elements.description: Current state of the decision record drawn from the governed state enumeration.

data_elements.name: status_history
data_elements.description: Ordered history of state transitions with actor, reason and RFC 3339 transition timestamp.

data_elements.name: became_final_at
data_elements.description: Time at which ordinary challenge routes were exhausted or expired.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The status model is a governed enumeration and transition table applied to the record, with each transition already evidenced by the immutable event-history artifact defined under f15. Duplicating that evidence as a second artifact would create two competing audit trails.

findings.name: Supersession, amendment, corrigendum and revocation
findings.description: How a later act changes or displaces this decision, distinguishing correction of the text from amendment of the substance and from withdrawal of the decision itself.

questions.text: Which change type applies — corrigendum to the text, amendment to the substance, replacement by a new decision, or revocation without replacement?
Which decision replaces this one and which does this one replace, expressed as explicit bidirectional links?
Does the change affect the whole decision or only identified parts, and does the remainder stay in force?
Who is competent to revoke or amend this decision, and must it be the same or a higher authority?
answer_data: Any procedural precondition such as a hearing

questions.text: From when does the change take effect, and does it disturb acts already taken in reliance on the original?
answer_data: Treatment of acts done in reliance

data_elements.name: change_type
data_elements.description: Whether the change is a corrigendum, an amendment, a replacement or a revocation.

data_elements.name: is_replaced_by
data_elements.description: Reference to the decision that supersedes this one.

data_elements.name: replaces
data_elements.description: Reference to the decision or decisions this one supersedes.

data_elements.name: invalidated_at
data_elements.description: Time from which the decision ceased to be usable or effective as a result of the change.

artifacts.name: Revoking, amending or correcting act
artifacts.description: The later instrument that corrects, amends, replaces or revokes this decision, itself an instance of this model and linked bidirectionally.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Carries its own canonical decision identifier from the issuing authority's series and cites the identifier of the decision it changes; the changed decision's identifier is never reassigned.

findings.name: Challenge, appeal, review and annulment
findings.description: The routes by which the decision can be contested, the time limits and suspensive effects that apply, and how the outcome of a challenge is recorded against the original.

questions.text: What challenge routes exist — internal review, administrative appeal, judicial review, ombudsman — and which apply to this decision?
answer_data: Available route list with forum references
Route stated in the decision notice

questions.text: What is the time limit for challenge, from which event does it run, and can it be extended?
answer_data: Computed deadline as an RFC 3339 timestamp

questions.text: Does lodging a challenge suspend the decision's effect, and if not can suspension be requested separately?
answer_data: Interim relief mechanism and its status

questions.text: How is the outcome of a challenge recorded — upheld, varied, quashed, remitted — and does it alter, replace or annul the original?
Where a decision is annulled, does the annulment operate from the original date or only from the annulment, and what happens to acts done meanwhile?

data_elements.name: challenge_routes
data_elements.description: Available contest routes with forum, deadline and suspensive effect.

data_elements.name: challenge_deadline
data_elements.description: Computed deadline by which a challenge must be lodged.

data_elements.name: challenges
data_elements.description: Lodged challenges with challenger, forum, lodging date, current state and outcome.

data_elements.name: review_outcome_effect
data_elements.description: Effect of a review outcome on the original decision, such as upheld, varied, quashed or remitted.

artifacts.name: Review or appeal decision
artifacts.description: The decision of the reviewing body disposing of a challenge, linked to the original decision and itself an instance of this model.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the reviewing forum's own decision identifier, using the governed global scheme where the forum is a court that participates in one; cites the challenged decision's identifier.

findings.name: Adjudicative grade and conclusiveness
findings.description: In hearings under APA § 557, a presiding employee may issue an initial decision that becomes the agency decision unless appealed or reviewed; otherwise a recommended or tentative decision may be required, except where the agency finds on the record that due and timely execution of its functions imperatively and unavoidably requires omission.

questions.text: Is this an initial, recommended, tentative or final agency decision, or does that grading not apply?
Did the deciding body preside at the reception of the evidence, and if not, who is the presiding or recommending employee?
Was the recommended or tentative decision omitted because the agency found on the record that due and timely execution of its functions imperatively and unavoidably required it?

data_elements.name: Decision grade
data_elements.description: Initial, recommended, tentative, final, or not-applicable.

data_elements.name: Presided at evidence flag
data_elements.description: Whether the deciding body received the evidence.

data_elements.name: Imperative omission flag
data_elements.description: Whether a recommended or tentative decision was omitted under the APA emergency clause.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Grade and conclusiveness are legal-state fields of the record. The supporting finding of imperative omission, if any, is text on this record rather than a new artefact type.

bundles.name: Relational context
bundles.description: The links that place a decision in its wider setting — the matter, occasion and prior decisions that produced it, and the parties and objects it acts upon.
bundles.rationale: A decision record with no outward links cannot be audited, aggregated or enforced. PROV-O supplies the generic derivation and association links, ECLI's metadata expectations imply citation links between decisions, and the registry's own CONTAINS and COMPOSE relations to the meeting and administrative-case models require explicit linkage semantics on this side.

layers.name: Contextual linkage
layers.description: Typed relationships from the decision to its procedural context, related decisions, addressees and subject objects.

findings.name: Relationships to matter, occasion and other decisions
findings.description: Typed links to the case or matter, the meeting or consent process that produced the decision, and prior, related, implementing and cited decisions.

questions.text: Which case, matter, project or programme contains this decision, and is containment exclusive?
answer_data: Position of the decision in the container's sequence

questions.text: Was the decision produced at a meeting or by a consent process, and which agenda item or consent round does it correspond to?
Which other decisions does this one implement, rely on, cite, contradict or depend on for its validity?
answer_data: Typed relation entries with target identifiers
Direction and required flag per relation

questions.text: What happens when a linked decision is revoked, annulled or destroyed under a retention rule — is this decision's validity affected?

data_elements.description: Reference to the case, matter or programme that contains the decision.

data_elements.name: occasion_reference

data_elements.name: decision_relations
data_elements.description: Typed links to other decisions with relation type, target identifier and whether the relation is required for validity.

Materialising them as an artifact would create a second, divergent copy of relationships that the referenced models already hold authoritatively.

findings.name: Addressees, affected parties and subject objects
findings.description: Who the decision is addressed to, who else it affects, and which concrete objects — assets, applications, permits, budgets, systems — it operates on.

questions.text: Who are the formal addressees of the decision, and how are they identified authoritatively rather than by name alone?
Which parties are affected without being addressees, and do they acquire procedural rights such as being heard or challenging?
Which objects does the decision operate on, and are they identified at a specific version or state?
answer_data: Version or state at decision time

questions.text: Does the decision produce legal or similarly significant effects on a natural person, and does that trigger additional safeguards?

data_elements.name: affected_parties

data_elements.name: subject_objects

findings.inline_only_rationale: Addressees and subject objects are references into party, asset and application models that own their master data. This finding governs only the linkage and the effect characterisation; holding a local artifact would duplicate party master data and create an unmanaged personal-data copy.

findings.name: Generating activity, used entities and derivation
findings.description: A decision record is a PROV entity generated by a deciding activity that used submissions, evidence, prior decisions, models or meeting records. Derivation and revision relate a later record to an earlier one without implying that usage alone is sufficient. Bundles support provenance of provenance.

questions.text: Which activity generated this decision record, and over what interval did that activity run?
Which evidence, submissions, prior decisions, models or other entities were used in making the decision?
From which prior records or drafts is this record derived or revised, and is a PROV bundle available for those assertions?

data_elements.name: Generating activity
data_elements.description: The PROV activity that produced the record.

data_elements.name: Used entities
data_elements.description: Inputs used by the deciding activity.

data_elements.name: Derived from
data_elements.description: Prior entities from which this record is derived.

artifacts.name: Provenance bundle
artifacts.description: Optional bundled provenance assertions about the decision record, enabling provenance of provenance.
artifacts.identity_strategy: PROV bundle identifier distinct from the decision entity identifier.

bundles.name: Automated and assisted decisioning
bundles.description: How much of the decision was made by a machine, which system and configuration produced it, and what human oversight, explanation and contestability attach as a result.
bundles.rationale: Where a decision is taken wholly or partly by a system, additional and legally consequential context becomes mandatory: the system's identity and version, the logic applied, human oversight, and the affected person's right to intervention, to express a point of view and to contest. GDPR Article 22, the Article 29 Working Party guidance and the AI Act's oversight and logging duties all attach to this distinction, and XACML supplies the structure of a machine-rendered decision result.

layers.name: Automation, oversight and explanation
layers.description: Decision mode and system attribution, and the oversight, explanation and contest mechanisms triggered by automation.

findings.name: Decision mode and system attribution
findings.description: Whether the decision was human, system-assisted or solely automated, and which system, model, policy version and inputs produced or shaped the result.

questions.text: Was the decision human-made, system-assisted or based solely on automated processing, and who assessed that classification?
Which system, model or rule engine produced or recommended the result, at which version and configuration?
Which policy, rule set or decision logic was applied, and is that exact version retained and retrievable?
What execution logs were generated, what do they contain, and for how long are they kept?
answer_data: Log retention period and its basis

questions.text: Where a human signed off a system-generated result, was that review substantive enough to displace 'solely automated' status?

data_elements.name: decision_mode
data_elements.description: Whether the decision was human, system-assisted or based solely on automated processing.

data_elements.name: deciding_system
data_elements.description: Reference to the system, model or engine that produced or recommended the result, with version.

data_elements.name: applied_policy_identifiers
data_elements.description: Identifiers and versions of the policies or rule sets evaluated in reaching the result.

data_elements.name: execution_log_reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the execution log or trace generated when the decision was rendered.

artifacts.name: Machine decision log entry
artifacts.description: The traceability record produced when a system renders a decision, capturing request attributes, applied policy identifiers, the decision value, status detail and any obligations returned.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the rendering system's identifier plus a monotonically increasing entry sequence and an RFC 3339 generation timestamp; correlated to the decision record by the canonical decision identifier where the result is retained as a record.

findings.name: Human oversight, explanation and contestability
findings.description: The oversight measures applied to an automated or assisted decision, the explanation owed to the affected person, and the mechanisms for intervention and contest.

questions.text: What human oversight measures applied, who exercised them, and did the overseer have authority and competence to change the outcome?
answer_data: Whether the outcome could in fact be overridden

questions.text: What explanation of the logic and of the significance and consequences is owed and provided to the affected person?
How can the affected person obtain human intervention, express a point of view and contest the decision, and what are the time limits?
Were any overrides of the system result recorded, by whom and on what stated ground?
answer_data: Override events with actor and ground

data_elements.name: oversight_measures
data_elements.description: Human oversight measures applied, with overseer reference and evidence of authority and competence.

data_elements.name: explanation_provided
data_elements.description: Explanation of the logic involved and of the significance and envisaged consequences, with delivery time.

data_elements.name: contest_mechanism

data_elements.name: override_events
